subject: science

applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public PYP page describes the programme as education for children aged 3-12. Mapping that span to Grade 2 (often about ages 7-8) is our convention, not an IB grade boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Grade 2 Florida science is still strongly observational (matter, weather, habitats, life cycles). It does not include the grade 3 library's star-and-space emphasis.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: The grade 3 library says PYP does not keep science as a separate subject and explores it through themes, especially How the world works and Sharing the planet. Public pages support transdisciplinary themes and subject-specific learning. The four science strand names below are reused from that grade 3 file.

concepts: Causation - Why is it like it is?
Connection - How is it connected to other things?
Perspective - What are the points of view?
global_contexts_or_transdisciplinary_the: Where we are in place and time

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The programme of inquiry is organized and framed by six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Although subjects play an important role in learning, PYP learners explore real-world problems by going beyond subject boundaries.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: PYP Science scope and sequence, as recorded in the grade 3 library, covers four strands: Living things, Earth and space, Materials and matter, and Forces and energy.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 2 Florida science in this draft has students raise questions and compare observations, describe properties and states of matter, investigate pushes, pulls, and magnets, discuss everyday energy use, observe rocks, soil, weather, and the Sun's warming, and compare needs, habitats, body parts, and life cycles. Those NGSSS benchmarks can be inquired into under How the world works and Sharing the planet. They are not IB learning outcomes.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Raising questions and investigating in teams fits inquiry and research skills. The Florida benchmark text is the requirement.
Distinguishing observation from inference fits thinking skills. It is not a published PYP phase outcome.
Solids, liquids, and gases fit the reused Materials and matter strand.
Pushes and pulls fit the reused Forces and energy strand.
Basic needs of living things fit Living things and can connect to Sharing the planet.
Repeating weather patterns fit Earth and space and the concept of change.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
